<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via getMetaItem (literal, a string literal in runAdminImportUsers))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via getMetaItem (literal, a string literal in runAdminImportUsers))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **34** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8532783f651a4a48b68e7d89579856e45501885e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d48846aac87b57b78b551ff6c2fbf94da4979843` — the merge of head `8c40d537f4a71d392b78e478c9d4225b5577a281` into base `8532783f651a4a48b68e7d89579856e45501885e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d48846aac87b57b78b551ff6c2fbf94da4979843 && git checkout d48846aac87b57b78b551ff6c2fbf94da4979843
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8532783f651a4a48b68e7d89579856e45501885e 8c40d537f4a71d392b78e478c9d4225b5577a281 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8532783f651a4a48b68e7d89579856e45501885e && git merge --no-ff 8c40d537f4a71d392b78e478c9d4225b5577a281

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8532783f651a4a48b68e7d89579856e45501885e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8532783f651a4a48b68e7d89579856e45501885e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8c40d537f4a71d392b78e478c9d4225b5577a281`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #22800 (body, claim 6110244295, file-surface addendum 6111285569, os-dev-reports 6111252864 and 6111748768); PR #22866 (body, the 5-file list, the net diff `origin/main...8c40d537f4`, merge-base `eed637c09f`); the 48 check-runs on the head, every one `success` or `skipped` and none failing (Check Changeset, Lint & Repo Gates, the four Type Check jobs, Test Core 1–6, Build Core, Dogfood Regression Gate, Governed Surface Queue Guard, the four PR-shape checks); the family precedent #22739 and its pending changeset on `origin/main`; the parent's census split 6102873261; and the `package.json` `exports` plus root `src/index.ts` of `packages/plugins/plugin-auth` and `packages/core` on `origin/main`, read only to judge what is published. Classes, positions and functions only.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The accept-set narrowing at the identity import door — right.** `runAdminImportUsers` (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users.ts`) binds `deps.getMetaItem` once as `metaReader` (:457–458) and spreads it into the run protocol literal (`const protocol: ImportProtocolLike`, :525, first member). In `packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts` at this head `p.getMetaItem` is read in exactly one place, `servesReferenceTarget` (:584–594), called once per target per import from `resolveRef` (:671). So the wiring implies exactly one behavioural change: a reference cell whose target's `enable` block does not serve `list` under `canServeApiOperation` answers `reference_not_found` for a match, a miss and a pasted id alike, and nothing of the target is read. No second rule — the card's direction, verbatim.
2. **No widening rides along — right.** `runImport` keys nothing else on the member; `prepareImportRequest` receives a reader of the same shape it received before (`p: metaReader` replaces an inline conditional spread of identical shape); the protocol literal declares no later `getMetaItem` that could override the spread (the symbol occurs at :165, :168, :457, :458 and :531 only). No adapter is written; the four Type Check jobs on the head accept the assignment as is.
3. **One `runImport` call, so the fix is complete at this door — right.** The file holds one `runImport(` call (:644) with that one protocol; the `manager_id` second pass (#18028) runs after `runImport` returns (:723) through the engine, not through a second protocol. The card's residual, a future `runImport` caller without the member, stays with the parent's close-out as the card assigns it.
4. **The fail-closed leg now applies here too — right, and correctly scoped.** `servesReferenceTarget` returns `false` only when the reader throws; a reader that answers with no `item` or no `enable` is read as no `enable` block, which `canServeApiOperation` serves. So the only new refusals at this door are targets whose own declaration refuses `list`, plus a throwing declaration read — the family's rule, unchanged. The measured population (`manager_id` into `sys_user`, stripped before `runImport`; `primary_business_unit_id` into `sys_business_unit`, default-open) moves no shipped answer; deployed extensions of `sys_user` are declared NOT MEASURED in the changeset and the PR body, which is the honest bound.
5. **The no-reader control is unchanged — right.** Without `deps.getMetaItem`, `metaReader` is `{}`, the parser builds no field map, no cell is a reference and the protocol carries no member; the `[#22800]` block's last control pins exactly this.
6. **Public surface of `@objectstack/plugin-auth` — a doc comment only, right.** `src/index.ts` on `origin/main` re-exports `./admin-import-users.js`, so `IdentityImportDeps` and `runAdminImportUsers` are published through the root entry (`exports["."]`, `dist/index.d.ts`). The diff changes `IdentityImportDeps.getMetaItem`'s TSDoc and no declaration: same optional member, same parameter and return types. No export added, removed or re-typed.
7. **Public surface of `@objectstack/core` — a doc comment only, right.** `src/index.ts` re-exports `./utils/import-runner.js`, so `ImportProtocolLike` is published through `exports["."]`. The diff rewords three TSDoc lines of its `getMetaItem` member (:214–216); the member's signature, the interface and every other line of the file are untouched. The retired sentence named plugin-auth's identity import as the example of a protocol without the member, which this PR makes false; the new sentence states the rule without the example and names the identity import as carrying it.
8. **Census pin, no `CALLERS` row — right.** `packages/core/src/security/second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts` keys its `CALLERS` table on files that call the arbiter `referenceTargetOf`, and the test reds a classified file that no longer calls it (the `stale` leg, :287) as well as an unclassified caller (:286). `admin-import-users.ts` never calls the arbiter; it takes its targets from `import-field-meta.ts`, already classified `decided` for the import door's `resolveRef` (:146–148). A row for this door would red the pin for the wrong reason. Naming the door in the docblock beside the row-8 MCP-bridge note (#22777), held by its own package's pin, is the shape row 8 used. Every `CALLERS` entry at this head is `decided`; there was no `open` row 9 to move, so the claim's "moves from open to decided" was an assumption the dev correctly falsified and declared.
9. **The pins are ablation-sensitive by construction — right.** The six `[#22800]` cases override only `find` and `getMetaItem` on `makeDeps`' pinned double. Without the protocol spread, `servesReferenceTarget` returns `true` at its first line, so the two refusing legs would answer `[OK, NOT_FOUND, OK]` instead of three `reference_not_found`, and the asked-through-the-reader leg would see one `getMetaItem` call instead of two; the three controls would stay green. That is the 3 red / 3 green the report records, and it follows from the code as read.
10. **Governed surfaces — none.** The five paths are under `.changeset/`, `packages/core/` and `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/`; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is green. The head repo is the base repo, so this is a delivery, not a fork proposal.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset `.changeset/22800-identity-import-exposure.md`:** `'@objectstack/plugin-auth': minor`; summary `fix(plugin-auth)!:`; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; exactly one `adr-0087:` marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, with the other categories closed on stated facts; the one-line BREAKING statement (an accept-set narrowing, shipped as `minor` under the launch-window convention); FROM and TO stated; measured producers and the NOT MEASURED bound stated; a one-line fix (grant `list` in `enable.apiMethods`, or drop `enable.apiEnabled: false`). This is the form of the family precedent `.changeset/22739-import-reference-target-exposure.md` on `origin/main` to the letter (`fix(core)!:`, `minor`, the same arm, the same marker category). `(narrowing)` is BREAKING under AGENTS.md's declaration rule; a breaking changeset carries its migration and exactly one ADR-0087 marker; `check-changeset-no-major` holds breaking bumps at `minor` — all met, and `Check Changeset` on the head is green. **Level: right.**
- **`Clause-②` agreement across the three carriers — right at this head.** PR body line 2 reads `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; the changeset reads `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; the card's binding declaration is the file-surface addendum 6111285569 (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `minor`, with an ADR-0087 disposition), written by the same seat as the claim. The original claim line (6110244295) read bare `no` with a "Narrowing:" bullet beneath it, which under-declared the arm the bullet itself described; the addendum corrected it before the head was cut, and the two reports record the switch (open question → answer B → round 1).
- **`no` is the right value:** the diff adds no authorable spelling, no export and no accepted input; it only narrows what the identity import accepts.
- **`@objectstack/core` has no changeset entry — right.** The core diff is a TSDoc reword inside a published `dist/index.d.ts`; no declaration, type, export or runtime line moves. AGENTS.md's changeset rule enumerates a feature, a functional improvement or a fix in a released package; a corrected doc comment is none of those, and `skip-changeset` is not in play (a changeset exists). `Check Changeset` on the head is green and `check-changeset-no-major` accepts the narrowing with core ungraded. The alternative the dev named (a `patch` entry, if a published comment counts as a publish) is not required: the behaviour the sentence now describes is recorded in the plugin-auth changeset, which is the package whose behaviour changed.

### ③ Boundary flags

Entries are named in listed order within each report.

**Report 6111252864 (round 0).**
- `open_questions`, the one entry — Clause-② arm (bare `no` + patch vs `no (narrowing)` + minor + ADR-0087). **Answered:** B, by the seat's addendum 6111285569, implemented at `8c40d537f4`; see ②.
- `out_of_scope_findings`, first — stale `ImportProtocolLike.getMetaItem` TSDoc in `import-runner.ts`. **Resolved in this PR:** the addendum widened the file surface by that one sentence (the `toFailedResult` region #22741 edits is disjoint; `No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path` is green), and the head carries the reword (:214–216, no other line).
- `out_of_scope_findings`, second — the pending `.changeset/22739-import-reference-target-exposure.md` Bindings bullet says the identity import "is not judged". **Escalated, non-blocking:** both changesets are unreleased, so `@objectstack/core`'s next CHANGELOG would name the identity import as a protocol without the member in the same release where `@objectstack/plugin-auth`'s says it carries it. That is an acceptance note (no defect, no contract violation, no authoring trap), but "no seat named" is not a carrier. This record names one: the adopting seat records it on #22661 at row 9's tick, as a one-line edit of that bullet's parenthetical, to ride the next family PR that touches `.changeset/` before the Version Packages PR is cut; the maintainer's release-notes pass is the fallback. Editing another card's pending changeset inside this PR would have been scope expansion, so leaving it out here was right.
- `deviations`, first — no `open` row 9 in the pin file; docblock naming instead. **Right**, per ①.8.
- `deviations`, second — pins in the existing test file on the pinned `makeDeps` double, after `check:engine-double-contract` flagged the first head's new double. **Right:** the double ledger is untouched and `Lint & Repo Gates` is green on the head.
- `deviations`, third — `origin/main` not merged. **Accepted:** the PR reads mergeable and clean; the head's checks ran on the merge ref; the merge-base is `eed637c09f` and the files main moved are disjoint from this diff's; the queue re-validates the joint tree.
- `deviations`, fourth — stale TSDoc left with a carrier because the dispatch forbade the file. **Superseded** by the round-1 reword (above).
- `deviations`, fifth — the harness attribution trailer was not imitated. **Right:** all four commits end with the model-free pair `Co-authored-by: Claude` and `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01ADzJtzYTLUfgrRZHxkagkX`, the form AGENTS.md prescribes for commits; no model identifier in title, body, changeset, comment or code.
- `deviations`, sixth — `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exit 3 then 0. **Accepted as a sequencing note:** `Build Core` and `Lint & Repo Gates` on the head are the verdict.

**Report 6111748768 (round 1, supersedes round 0).**
- `open_questions` — none.
- `out_of_scope_findings`, the one entry — the #22739 changeset sentence. **Same escalation as above.**
- `pr_body_false_sentences` (8 entries) — not a flag class, but checked: the PR body at review time already carries every replacement (final head `8c40d537f4`; "no code in core or rest changes; the one core edit is a TSDoc sentence"; lint on 4 files; 68 gates; main at `8532783f65`; the reworded-TSDoc and `no (narrowing)` acceptance notes). **Reconciled.**
- `deviations`, first — worktree recreated on the same branch at `49e162847a`. **Process note, accepted.**
- `deviations`, second — `origin/main` not merged, 9 commits, disjoint. **Accepted**, as above.
- `deviations`, third — `dual-build-cjs-loads` sequencing. **Accepted**, as above.
- `deviations`, fourth — `@objectstack/core` not added to the changeset; "if the seat reads 'ships in dist/index.d.ts' as published, the level would be patch". **Answered: no entry**, per ②.
- `deviations`, fifth — labels `documentation`, `size/m`, `tests`, `tooling` set by the labeler, left alone. **Right:** state another actor set is not the dev's to correct.

**Residuals carried, none blocking:** (a) the #22739 changeset parenthetical, escalated above; (b) a future `runImport` caller without the member, which the card assigns to the parent's close-out; (c) deployed or cloud-held extensions of `sys_user`, declared NOT MEASURED in the changeset and the PR body.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-22800-identity-import-exposure`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ADzJtzYTLUfgrRZHxkagkX`

**VERDICT: PASS**
